# Hermes Proactive Agent - Full Reference

> Hermes Proactive Agent (`proactive-agent`) is an MIT-licensed Hermes Agent plugin that governs how a chat-based AI assistant delegates work. It keeps the main agent responsive with a per-turn time budget (60 s reminder, 120 s edit/execute pause), moves foreground terminal commands longer than 30 s to the background through Hermes' own yield path, returns `delegate_task` briefs under 120 characters once per turn and enriches accepted briefs with chat context and memory, stops a subagent that produces the same tool outcome 5 times, brings open decisions and refused commands back to the main agent as `needs_decision`, verifies each reported result, keeps background results marked unreported until an uninterrupted reply delivers them to the user, and persists every task in a SQLite ledger at `<hermes home>/plugin-data/proactive-agent/ledger.db` (retaining the last 20 finished tasks per chat for up to 7 days). The plugin makes zero model calls, never writes directly into the user's chat, and fails open on internal errors.

This file is the complete, self-contained technical reference for the project. It is maintained alongside `README.md` from the same verified codebase facts; when any wording differs, the source code under `proactive-agent/` is authoritative.

- Repository: https://github.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-proactive-agent
- Version: 0.1.16 · License: MIT · Language: Python 3.10+ · Runtime dependencies: none
- Host requirement: Hermes Agent >= 0.22 (tested on v0.22.7)
- Verification commands: `uv run --group dev pytest` and `uv run --group dev ruff check`

## Question index

Every question below is answered in full in the "Mechanism detail" and "FAQ" sections.

1. How do you stop a Hermes Agent chat from going silent while it works?
2. How do you keep a long build or test run from blocking a chat turn?
3. Why do subagents start without context, and how do you brief them properly?
4. How do you stop subagents from repeating the same failing tool call forever?
5. Can a subagent ask the user a question, and what happens when command approval refuses a step?
6. How do you make an agent's "done" claim verifiable instead of a self-report?
7. What happens when the user sends a message right as a background subagent result arrives?
8. How do you persist subagent task results across a Hermes gateway restart?
9. Does this plugin call a model or add token cost?
10. Which platforms and sessions does the plugin govern?
11. What happens if the plugin itself raises an error?

## What it is

Hermes Proactive Agent is a lightweight host plugin, not a separate agent framework or runtime. It registers ten lifecycle hooks on Hermes (`pre_llm_call`, `pre_api_request`, `pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call`, `transform_tool_result`, `subagent_start`, `subagent_stop`, `on_session_end`, `on_session_reset`, `on_session_finalize`) plus one system prompt section (`proactive-agent.discipline`), filling only the gaps Hermes leaves open when used from a messaging app.

The core model in one sentence: **the main agent acts like a secretary and subagents act like workers.** The secretary stays reachable in chat, makes decisions, and reports back; workers handle the slow jobs in the background; every job ends with a checked, recorded result that reaches the user.

Three design invariants govern the entire codebase:

- **Talk only to the main agent.** The plugin attaches notes to the main agent's context and, when a report was cut short by a new user message, wakes the main agent with an internal message (`ctx.inject_message`). It never posts directly to the user's chat.
- **No model calls.** Every check is deterministic Python code with zero inference latency.
- **Never in the way.** Every hook is wrapped in `_guarded`: any unexpected plugin exception is logged and the call proceeds normally.

## Install

```bash
hermes plugins install JerryLiu369/hermes-proactive-agent/proactive-agent
hermes plugins enable proactive-agent
```

The plugin id is `proactive-agent`. The install path `JerryLiu369/hermes-proactive-agent/proactive-agent` points to the plugin subdirectory, which is the only directory Hermes copies during installation. Restart the gateway after enabling, and update later with `hermes plugins update proactive-agent`.

Recommended host settings in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:

- `delegation.max_iterations: 60` caps total subagent iterations so a wandering subagent reports back sooner.
- `plugins.entries.proactive-agent.allow_gateway_injection: true` grants Hermes' permission for `ctx.inject_message`, allowing the plugin to wake the main agent when a user message interrupts a background result report (without it, the reminder simply rides on the user's next message). Use the plugin id shown by `hermes plugins list` if installed under another name:

```yaml
delegation:
  max_iterations: 60
plugins:
  entries:
    proactive-agent:
      allow_gateway_injection: true
```

Verify the plugin is active:

```bash
hermes plugins list           # proactive-agent should appear as enabled
```

## Status quo vs governed: comparison matrix

"Status quo" describes vanilla Hermes Agent with subagent delegation enabled and this plugin disabled.

| Dimension | Status quo | Governed by proactive-agent |
|---|---|---|
| Main-agent turn duration | Unbounded; the chat goes silent until the turn finishes | Soft reminder at 60 s; hard pause on edit/execute tools at 120 s; resets when the user writes mid-turn |
| Tools available after 120 s | Unchanged | `read_file`, `search_files`, `session_search`, `vision_analyze`, `memory`, `skill_view`, `skills_list`, `skill_manage`, `todo_list`, `clarify`, `delegate_task`, and `process_manage` (`list`/`poll`/`log`/`kill`) |
| Long foreground terminal command | Blocks the turn until exit or timeout | Auto-detached to the background at 30 s via `BaseEnvironment._wait_for_process` + `tools.interrupt.request_yield`; process keeps running |
| Signal when a command is detached | Raw `yielded_to_background` payload | Explicit note that the command is still running in the background, has not failed, and will notify when done |
| Blocking on a background process | `process_manage(action='wait')` allowed | Refused immediately so waiting cannot freeze the chat |
| Brief quality gate | `delegate_task` accepts any `context` | `context` shorter than 120 characters is returned once per turn with instructions on what to add |
| File write contention across subagents | Undetected | A brief naming a file another running subagent is modifying is returned once per turn |
| Subagent starting context | Empty (`skip_memory=True`, no chat history) | Appended briefing: last 6 user messages verbatim, `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md`, running subagents and their files, recent unfinished tasks, working rules, default `output_schema` |
| Repeated identical tool outcomes | Hermes warns subagents but never stops them | Cumulative counter across the whole run: warn on 3rd identical outcome, hard stop on 5th, refuse further tools, require `blocked` report |
| Outcome matching for repeats | Consecutive tool calls | Whole-run history matched by tool name, arguments, and first result line with long numbers and hashes masked |
| Decisions outside a subagent's scope | No `clarify` tool and no resume; subagent guesses or aborts | Subagent stops with `needs_decision`, `question`, and `options`; main agent answers from chat/memory or asks the user in one message, then spawns a follow-up subagent |
| Step refused by approval or hook | Subagent may retry or search for a workaround | Immediate note (or on next tool result for a hook): do not retry or work around it; if required for the goal, report `needs_decision` |
| Result verification | "Done" is an unchecked self-report | Next main-agent turn opens with reported evidence, or warns on missing evidence, unfinished status, or repeat stop |
| Background result arrives while user types | Hermes merges the user's message into the reporting turn; main agent often answers only the message | Result stays marked unreported until an uninterrupted reply completes: reminded via next tool result, woken via `inject_message` (max 2 wakes), or reminded on the user's next message |
| Task durability and retention | Lost when subagent exits or gateway restarts | SQLite ledger (`ledger.db`) stores goal, status, files, steers, transcript path, summary, evidence, blockers, and open questions; keeps last 20 finished tasks per chat for up to 7 days |
| Gateway restart mid-task | Running subagents vanish silently | Interrupted tasks are marked `lost`; next turn tells the main agent which tasks were lost, which files they touched, and that side effects are unknown |
| Failure mode of the plugin | N/A | Fails open: exceptions are logged and never block a tool call |
| Model calls / token overhead | N/A | Zero model calls; compact context notes only |
| Governed scope | N/A | Only `governed_platforms` (default `["weixin"]`) and their subagents; cron, CLI, and other platforms untouched |

## Mechanism detail

### 1. The chat stays responsive (`secretary.py`)

The main agent may investigate and decide directly, but each turn has a time budget divided into three zones:

| Zone | Threshold | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `green` | `0 s` | Normal execution |
| `yellow` | `turn_soft_seconds` = `60 s` | One note attached to the next tool result: answer the user or delegate within 1-2 steps |
| `red` | `turn_hard_seconds` = `120 s` | Editing and execution tools are refused for the rest of the turn; reading, `delegate_task`, and wrap-up tools remain available |

- **Mid-turn user messages reset the clock.** When the user writes while a turn is running, Hermes delivers the message either as a steer (`[OUT-OF-BAND USER MESSAGE` or `display_kind: "steer"`) or as an active-turn redirect (`[This response was interrupted by a user correction.]`). On `pre_api_request`, `secretary.on_api_request` detects new interjections, adds them to the stored user messages, and resets the turn timer back to `green`.
- **Context compression is not counted.** Hermes fires `pre_auxiliary_call` and `post_auxiliary_call` around each auxiliary model call with the parent turn's `session_id` and `turn_id`. For `aux_task == "compression"` in the running turn, `secretary.on_compression` stops the clock at the first call and moves the turn start forward by the time spent when the last one returns. Other auxiliary calls (vision, titles) and calls from another turn (such as the background review) keep the clock running.
- **Allowed tools in the red zone:** `read_file`, `search_files`, `session_search`, `vision_analyze`, `delegate_task`, `memory`, `skill_view`, `skills_list`, `skill_manage`, `todo_list`, `clarify`, and `process_manage` limited to actions `list`, `poll`, `log`, and `kill`.
- **Single notification per zone:** Each zone transition is announced at most once per turn so tool results are never spammed.

### 2. Long commands move to the background (`secretary.py`)

Instead of killing slow commands or wrapping them in shell hacks, the plugin hooks into Hermes' native process-yield path. It wraps `BaseEnvironment._wait_for_process` and, only when called on a governed main-agent tool thread, starts a timer for `terminal_auto_detach_seconds` (default `30 s`). When the timer fires while the process is still running, it calls `tools.interrupt.request_yield(watch_interrupt_tid)`. Hermes detaches the running process to the background and returns `status: "yielded_to_background"`.

`secretary.transform_tool_result` then attaches a clear `note` field to the JSON tool result explaining that the command ran longer than 30 s, moved to the background, has **not** failed, holds its partial stdout in `output`, and will notify the agent automatically when it finishes. Any late yield signal is cleaned up via `consume_yield` in a `finally` block so subsequent commands on the same thread are never affected.

In addition, `process_manage(action='wait')` is blocked in `pre_tool_call` because synchronous waiting would freeze the chat turn again.

### 3. Subagents start informed (`handoff.py`)

Because Hermes runs subagents with `skip_memory=True` and no conversation history, the main agent is responsible for writing each subagent's brief. `handoff.gate` inspects `delegate_task(action='spawn')` calls and returns the call **once per turn** (a second attempt in the same turn always passes) in two situations:

1. **Thin context:** any task's `context` is shorter than `handoff_min_context_chars` (default `120` characters). The refusal asks the main agent to include what is already known, exact targets, what must not change, when to stop, and what evidence proves success.
2. **File clash:** a task's `goal` or `context` names a file path that another currently running subagent in the same chat has already modified. The refusal suggests waiting, steering the running worker with `delegate_task(action='steer')`, or stopping it with `delegate_task(action='stop')`.

Every accepted task has a structured handoff briefing appended after the main agent's own `context`:

| Briefing section | Purpose |
|---|---|
| The user's last 6 messages, verbatim | Preserves exact user wording and negative constraints such as "don't touch X" |
| `USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` | Supplies user preferences and environment facts that Hermes skips for subagents |
| Other subagents running now | Lists active sibling goals, elapsed minutes, and files they are modifying |
| Earlier unfinished work in this chat | Up to 3 recent non-completed tasks (within 24 h): status, summary, blockers, open question, `steer` corrections, modified files, and live transcript path |
| Working rules | Stay in scope; stop after the same failure twice; report `needs_decision` instead of guessing; never work around a refused command; require a rollback path for risky changes; do not edit another worker's files; verify the real end state |
| Default `output_schema` | Enforces `status` (`completed`, `partial`, `blocked`, `needs_decision`, `failed`), `summary`, `evidence`, `blockers`, and `question` (required when `status == "needs_decision"`) plus `options`, unless the caller provided a custom schema |

### 4. Subagents do not spin or guess (`workers.py`, `handoff.py`, `reports.py`)

**Cumulative repeat guard:** Hermes' built-in loop guard warns subagents on repeated calls but does not hard-stop them. `workers.post_tool_call` tracks `(call_signature(tool_name, args), result_signature(result))` across the subagent's entire run. `result_signature` normalizes the first line of the outcome by masking numbers of 4+ digits and hex hashes of 8+ characters, so changing timestamps, PIDs, or request IDs still match. With `worker_repeat_limit` set to `5` (default):

- At the **3rd** identical outcome (`limit - 2`), a warning note is attached to the tool result telling the worker to change approach or report the blocker.
- At the **5th** identical outcome (`limit`), `stop_reason` is set and a `STOP` note is attached. Any subsequent `pre_tool_call` from that worker is blocked, forcing it to conclude with status `blocked`.

**Structured decisions and refused commands:** Subagents have no `clarify` tool and cannot be resumed once they finish. When a subagent encounters an unresolved choice that belongs to the main agent or user, its working rules and `DEFAULT_OUTPUT_SCHEMA` instruct it to stop and report `status: "needs_decision"` with `question` and `options`. Hermes validates the final output against the JSON schema and grants one correction turn if `question` is omitted.

When Hermes' command approval refuses a subagent call (returning an error starting with `BLOCKED`) or leaves a terminal call in `status: "pending_approval"`, `workers.transform_tool_result` attaches an immediate note instructing the worker not to retry, rephrase, or work around the refusal, and to report `needs_decision` if the step is required. If a shell hook or plugin blocks a call in `pre_tool_call` (`error_type == "plugin_block"`), Hermes skips `transform_tool_result`, so `workers.post_tool_call` queues the same note for the worker's next tool result. The note also explains that a "user denied" message may be automatic (`delegation.subagent_auto_approve: false` in CLI mode).

When the subagent finishes with `needs_decision`, `reports.on_subagent_stop` queues a note for the main agent containing the question and options. Because the main agent can see the full conversation and memory, it resolves the question itself if the answer is already settled, or asks the user in one concise message, and then dispatches a new subagent with the answer (which automatically receives the unfinished task's ledger record). If the user has heard the question and the main agent still has not dispatched a follow-up by the user's next message, `_decision_reminder` reminds the main agent once.

### 5. Results are checked, delivered, and remembered (`reports.py`, `ledger.py`)

**Verification notes:** When `subagent_stop` fires, `reports.on_subagent_stop` parses the worker's structured report, extracts written file paths from `tool_call_history`, closes the task in the ledger, and queues a note for the main agent's next turn:

- `completed` with `evidence`: lists the evidence items and reminds the main agent to spot-check the real state.
- `completed` without `evidence`: warns that success was claimed without proof.
- Stopped by repeat guard: tells the main agent why the plugin stopped the worker and instructs it to tell the user in one line what got stuck and what it will do instead.
- Stopped intentionally by the main agent (`delegate_task(action='stop')`): recorded as `stopped` rather than a failure.

**Guaranteed delivery of background results:** Background tasks (`status: "dispatched"` on `delegate_task`) deliver their completion in a separate async-delegation turn. If the user sends a message while that turn is running, Hermes redirects or steers the turn, and the main agent frequently answers only the user's new message while dropping the background report. The plugin tracks every background result as `unreported = True` in the ledger until a turn that displayed it finishes (`completed=True`) with no unanswered mid-turn user interjections:

| Turn scenario | Plugin action |
|---|---|
| Turn completes with no mid-turn user message | `ledger.settle` marks the result as heard (`unreported = False`) |
| User writes mid-turn, then the main agent calls a tool | `reports.tool_result_note` appends a reminder to that tool result: answer the user and report the finished task in the same reply |
| User writes mid-turn, and the main agent replies without calling a tool | `reports.on_turn_end` calls `ctx.inject_message` (up to `_MAX_WAKES = 2` times per result) to queue an internal wake turn; the main agent reports briefly or replies `[SILENT]` if already covered |
| Turn is interrupted/failed, or gateway injection is disabled | The result stays `unreported` and is attached to the start of the user's next turn |

**Durable SQLite ledger and restart recovery:** `ledger.py` stores two tables (`tasks` and `notes`) in `<hermes home>/plugin-data/proactive-agent/ledger.db`:

- Each `tasks` row stores `id`, `parent`, `child`, `status`, `started`, `ended`, `pid`, and a JSON `data` payload (`goal`, `files`, `steers`, `transcript`, `summary`, `evidence`, `blockers`, `background`, `unreported`, `shown`, `shown_turn`, `wakes`, `question`, `options`, `awaiting`, `asked_turn`).
- Retention is bounded automatically: up to **20 finished tasks** per chat (`_KEEP_FINISHED_PER_PARENT = 20`), expiring records older than **7 days** (`_KEEP_SECONDS = 7 * 86400`), and chasing unreported results for at most **24 hours** (`_REPORT_HORIZON_S = 86400`).
- On startup (`ledger.load` / `reports.recover_lost`), any task left in `running` status by a dead gateway PID is atomically claimed, marked `lost` and `unreported`, and queued as a warning note for that chat's next turn listing the interrupted goal and the files it had already touched.

## Configuration

Settings live under `plugins.entries.proactive-agent.settings` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`. Resolution order is: environment variable `PROACTIVE_<KEY>` (uppercase), then `config.yaml`, then `config.DEFAULTS`.

```yaml
plugins:
  entries:
    proactive-agent:
      allow_gateway_injection: true   # Hermes host permission for ctx.inject_message
      settings:
        governed_platforms: ["weixin"]
        turn_soft_seconds: 60
        turn_hard_seconds: 120
        terminal_auto_detach_seconds: 30
        handoff_min_context_chars: 120
        worker_repeat_limit: 5
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description | Environment override |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `governed_platforms` | `list[str]` | `["weixin"]` | Platforms whose main agent and spawned subagents are governed | `PROACTIVE_GOVERNED_PLATFORMS` |
| `turn_soft_seconds` | `float` | `60` | Seconds before the main agent is reminded to answer or delegate | `PROACTIVE_TURN_SOFT_SECONDS` |
| `turn_hard_seconds` | `float` | `120` | Seconds before editing and command execution pause for the rest of the turn | `PROACTIVE_TURN_HARD_SECONDS` |
| `terminal_auto_detach_seconds` | `int` | `30` | Seconds before a foreground terminal command moves to the background (`0` disables) | `PROACTIVE_TERMINAL_AUTO_DETACH_SECONDS` |
| `handoff_min_context_chars` | `int` | `120` | Minimum `delegate_task` `context` length; shorter briefs are returned once per turn | `PROACTIVE_HANDOFF_MIN_CONTEXT_CHARS` |
| `worker_repeat_limit` | `int` | `5` | Identical tool outcomes before a subagent is stopped (warned two attempts earlier) | `PROACTIVE_WORKER_REPEAT_LIMIT` |

## Compatibility and limits

- **Host:** Hermes Agent >= 0.22 (verified against v0.22.7 source).
- **Runtime:** Python >= 3.10, zero external runtime dependencies.
- **Test matrix:** `ruff check` and `pytest` on Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14; `tests/test_hermes_e2e.py` exercises the real Hermes plugin loader when `hermes_cli` is available.
- **No subagent resume in Hermes:** Hermes cannot resume a finished subagent session. Continuity is provided by briefing the next subagent in the same chat with the unfinished task's ledger record.
- **Step budget ownership:** Total subagent iteration limits remain controlled by Hermes' `delegation.max_iterations`.
- **Process-local vs durable state:** Active turn timers and running-worker repeat counters live in memory per gateway process; task records, queued notes, open questions, and unreported-result flags persist in SQLite across restarts.

## FAQ

**How do I stop a Hermes Agent chat from going silent while it works?**
Install and enable `proactive-agent`. The main agent receives a reminder at 60 s to reply or delegate, and loses edit/execute tools at 120 s for the remainder of the turn. Sending a new message mid-turn resets the timer.

**How do I keep a 10-minute build from blocking my chat?**
Any governed foreground terminal command still running after 30 s is automatically detached to the background through Hermes' yield mechanism. The command keeps running, the main agent is told it has not failed, and Hermes notifies the chat when it completes. `process_manage(action='wait')` is refused so the agent cannot block on it.

**Why does my subagent not know what we discussed in chat, and how does the plugin fix it?**
Hermes spawns subagents with `skip_memory=True` and no chat history. The plugin gates `delegate_task` briefs shorter than 120 characters once per turn and appends the user's last 6 messages verbatim, `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md`, active sibling subagents, recent unfinished tasks, working rules, and a structured `output_schema`.

**How do I stop a subagent from repeating the same failing tool call until its budget runs out?**
The plugin counts identical `(tool, args, normalized_first_line)` outcomes across the whole subagent run, warns on the 3rd repeat, and stops the subagent on the 5th, refusing further tool calls so it must report `blocked`. Pairing this with `delegation.max_iterations: 60` catches non-identical wandering loops as well.

**Can a subagent ask the user a question, and what happens when command approval refuses a step?**
Subagents cannot call `clarify` or be resumed. Instead, when a subagent hits a decision outside its authority, or when Hermes' approval or a hook refuses a command it needs, it stops and reports `status: "needs_decision"` with a `question` and `options` (and is explicitly told on the spot not to work around a refusal). The main agent answers the question itself when the chat or memory settles it, or asks the user in one short message, then dispatches a new subagent briefed with the answer and the earlier task's record.

**How do I verify a subagent actually finished the job?**
Every accepted task receives a default `output_schema` requiring `status`, `summary`, `evidence`, and `blockers`. When the subagent stops, the main agent's next turn opens with the reported evidence or an explicit warning if evidence is missing, the task is incomplete, or the worker was stopped for looping.

**What happens when the user sends a message right as a background subagent result arrives?**
The background result stays marked `unreported` until a turn that showed it finishes with an uninterrupted reply. If the main agent calls a tool after the user's message, that tool result reminds it to answer the user and report the finished task together; if it replies without calling a tool, the plugin wakes it via `ctx.inject_message` (requires `allow_gateway_injection: true`) for a brief follow-up or `[SILENT]`; otherwise the reminder rides on the user's next message.

**How do I persist task progress across a Hermes gateway restart?**
Every task, pending note, and unreported-result flag is stored in SQLite at `<hermes home>/plugin-data/proactive-agent/ledger.db`. If the gateway restarts while a subagent is running, the plugin marks the task `lost` and tells the main agent on the next turn which tasks were interrupted and which files they had touched.

**Does this plugin make extra model calls or cost tokens?**
It makes zero model calls of its own; it only adds concise notes to the main agent's context and subagent briefings. Waking the main agent after an interrupted report uses one extra turn, equivalent to one user message.

**Will it interfere with cron jobs, the CLI, or other chat platforms?**
No. Only platforms listed in `governed_platforms` (default `["weixin"]`) and the subagents they spawn are governed. Cron runs, CLI sessions, and unlisted platforms are untouched.

**What if two subagents try to edit the same file?**
A `delegate_task` call whose `goal` or `context` names a file another running subagent is already modifying is returned once per turn so the main agent can wait, steer the active worker, or stop it.
